audits.title: Asthma care in Darley Dale: general practitioner audit.
audits.standard: Recording of asthma diagnosis, peak flow, smoking history, review, medication and admissions

cycle1.result: Asthma on computer problem list 93/161 (58%); at least one peak flow 24/161 (15%); three or more peak flows 15/161 (9%); smoking history 24/161 (15%); reviewed at least once 61/161 (38%).

audits.intervention: Nurse-run asthma clinic set up in the practice.

cycle2.result: Asthma on problem list 233/238 (98%); at least one peak flow 143/238 (60%); three or more 40/238 (17%); smoking history 133/238 (56%); reviewed at least once 74/238 (31%).

audits.other_findings: No significant change in reviews, long-term medication recording, acute treatment or peak flow ratio; no objective improvement in asthma detected.
audits.citation: Martys CR. Asthma care in Darley Dale: general practitioner audit. BMJ. 1992;304(6829):758-760. doi:10.1136/bmj.304.6829.758. PMID: 1530691.

audits.title: Impact of the Singapore National Asthma Program (SNAP) on preventor-reliever prescription ratio in polyclinics.
audits.standard: Preventor-reliever prescription ratio as key performance indicator (Singapore National Asthma Program)
audits.intervention: Audit and positive feedback on PR ratio plus local initiatives (chronic care models, multidisciplinary teams, decision support tools, self-management support, patient information system, community education)
audits.other_findings: Asthma case load in the polyclinics increased by 31% over the programme.
audits.citation: Chong PN, Tan NC, Lim TK. Impact of the Singapore National Asthma Program (SNAP) on preventor-reliever prescription ratio in polyclinics. Ann Acad Med Singap. 2008;37(2):114-117. PMID: 18327346.

audits.title: Measuring success in asthma care: a repeat audit.

cycle1.result: Baseline asthma care measures (figures not given).

audits.intervention: Minimal intervention programme using checklists, booklets and repeated audit.

cycle2.result: Significant increase in peak flow meter ownership and use and improved inhaler technique; inadequate control in 22%.

audits.other_findings: Significant improvements in night-time symptoms in children (P < 0.05) and daytime symptoms in adults (P < 0.001).
audits.citation: Barritt PW, Staples EB. Measuring success in asthma care: a repeat audit. Br J Gen Pract. 1991;41(347):232-236. PMID: 1931201.

audits.title: Quality of asthma care: Western Cape province, South Africa.
audits.standard: South African guidelines for chronic asthma in adults and adolescents
audits.setting: 46 primary care facilities, six districts of the Western Cape

cycle1.result: 11.5% of visits assessed control; PEF recorded 23.2%; inhaler technique assessed 14%; self-management plan 11.2%; 31.5% well controlled.

audits.other_findings: Only 80% had a consistent asthma diagnosis; 81% of medication in stock; controller/reliever ratio 0.6.
audits.citation: Mash B, Rhode H, Pather M, Ainslie G, Irusen E, Bheekie A, et al.. Quality of asthma care: Western Cape province, South Africa. S Afr Med J. 2009;99(12):892-896. PMID: 20460001.

audits.title: An audit of inhaler technique among asthma patients of 34 general practitioners.
audits.standard: Inhaler technique scoring system (good 4/4, adequate 3-4, inadequate 2 or less)
audits.setting: 34 general practices (St George's Hospital Medical School, London)

cycle1.result: 25% had inadequate technique; good technique 78% with Turbohaler and 45% with metered dose inhalers.

audits.other_findings: 63% used metered dose inhalers, 15% Rotahalers, 9% spacers.
audits.citation: Hilton S. An audit of inhaler technique among asthma patients of 34 general practitioners. Br J Gen Pract. 1990;40(341):505-506. PMID: 2282229.

audits.title: Large care gaps in primary care management of asthma: a longitudinal practice audit.
audits.standard: Evidence-based adult asthma practices: symptom-based asthma control assessment, controller escalation, written action plan
audits.setting: Three family health teams (two academic, one community), Ontario

cycle1.result: Asthma control assessed in 4.9% of visits and 15.4% of patients; controller escalated in 3.3% of visits.

audits.other_findings: Assessment was more frequent at visits for asthma symptoms (35.0%) than other visits (1.6%).
audits.citation: Price C, Agarwal G, Chan D, Goel S, Kaplan AG, Boulet LP, et al.. Large care gaps in primary care management of asthma: a longitudinal practice audit. BMJ Open. 2019;9(1):e022506. doi:10.1136/bmjopen-2018-022506. PMID: 30696669.

audits.title: Collaborative quality improvement initiative to enhance adult asthma management.
audits.standard: Asthma management guidelines: Asthma Action Plan reviewed within 12 months
audits.setting: Family medicine clinic, Mayo Clinic, Arizona

cycle1.result: Updated Asthma Action Plan 7.5%; optimal asthma control 40.0%.

audits.intervention: Multidisciplinary intervention: nursing review of problem lists, pre-visit Asthma Management Questionnaire and Asthma Control Test via portal or rooming, and clinician completion of action plans.

cycle2.result: Updated Asthma Action Plan 43.4%; optimal asthma control 66.4%.

audits.citation: Sharma R, Brandse SK, Riffle TL. Collaborative quality improvement initiative to enhance adult asthma management. BMJ Open Qual. 2025;14(2):e003265. doi:10.1136/bmjoq-2024-003265. PMID: 40425204.

audits.title: An audit of asthma in a Belfast practice.

cycle1.result: Regular peak expiratory flow monitoring in just 14%; 13 diagnostic labels used; inadequate treatment in a small number of patients.

audits.other_findings: Up to five different diagnostic labels used for a single patient.
audits.citation: Clarke KE, Irwin WG. An audit of asthma in a Belfast practice. Ulster Med J. 1985;54(2):160-164. PMID: 4095804.

audits.title: The national asthma audit. Bridging the gap between guidelines and practice.

cycle1.result: Asthma review recorded in past 12 months in 177 (72.8%); regular preventive therapy in 138 (56.8%); asthma action plan in 118 (48.2%).

audits.other_findings: Results discussed at a peer workshop; 15 of 16 respondents (93.8%) said the audit motivated them to change practice.
audits.citation: Collins S, Beilby J, Fardy J, Burgess T, Johns R, Booth B. The national asthma audit. Bridging the gap between guidelines and practice. Aust Fam Physician. 1998;27(10):907-913. PMID: 9798289.
